attachments.origin_landmark: superior border of the rib below (inner surface), from sternum/costal cartilage to rib angle
attachments.insertion_landmark: inferior border of the rib above

actions: interchondral (parasternal) part elevates the sternal ribs (assists inspiration)

functional_compartments.name: Interosseous part
functional_compartments.function_note: Runs from the rib angles anteriorly to the costochondral junctions; fibers oriented opposite to the overlying external intercostals (inferolateral to superomedial). Its documented action is expiratory (depresses ribs), unlike the interchondral part of the same named muscle.
functional_compartments.source: De Troyer A, Kirkwood PA, Wilson TA (2005) Physiol Rev 85(2):717-756 -- respiratory action and regional functional differences of the intercostal muscles

functional_compartments.name: Interchondral (parasternal) part
functional_compartments.function_note: Short segment between adjacent costal cartilages, anterior to the interosseous part; despite being part of the same named muscle it is documented to act as an inspiratory rib elevator -- a clear real example of one named muscle containing two regions with opposite mechanical actions.
functional_compartments.source: De Troyer A, Kirkwood PA, Wilson TA (2005) Physiol Rev 85(2):717-756 -- respiratory action and regional functional differences of the intercostal muscles

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); De Troyer A, Kirkwood PA, Wilson TA (2005) Physiol Rev 85(2):717-756 -- respiratory action and regional functional differences of the intercostal muscles
